chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him (peace be upon him): 'A man marries his slave girl to a free man, then he wants to remove her from him and take from him half the dower.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who married her to him sees what you are upon and makes a religion by it, then for him is that he removes her from him and takes from him half the dower, because he has proceeded from that upon the understanding that that is for the master. And if the husband does not know this, and he is from the masses of the people, the master would deal with him upon what he deals with one similar to him, so he has proceeded upon the understanding of that from him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a master wants to take back his slave wife from her free husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the master's right to annul the marriage of his slave girl to a free man, contingent upon whether the husband was aware of this specific legal prerogative or falls under the general public who are treated according to common custom. It highlights the Shia juristic distinction between explicit knowledge of the master's right and the default assumption of customary practice, ensuring the master recovers half the dower in either scenario.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man married his slave girl to a free man, then he wanted to remove her from him, and take from him half the dower’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If the one who married her to him were to see what you all are upon and makes a religion by it, so for him is then he removes her from him, and takes from him half the dower, because he has proceeded from that upon the understanding that, that is the for master (to do), and if the husband does not understand this, and he is from the masses of the people, the master would deal with him upon what he deals with one similar to him, so he has preceded upon the understanding of that from him’.
